interface.title: Lemmata — Multilingual Topic Modeling (v0.1.0, Streamlit)
interface.field: Digital humanities / computational literary studies (text mining)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory analysis of a text corpus, then judging model quality and exporting results for publication
interface.what_it_is_for: Fit an LDA topic model to uploaded literary texts after language-aware lemmatization and part-of-speech filtering, then inspect topics, their spread across text chunks, the coherence score and a token-level preprocessing trace, and export the results in a reproducible form.

data.note: Uploaded svevo_senilita.txt (Italian, about 65,681 words), which the app split into 67 chunks of about 1,000 words. Settings: language Italian, POS preset Content words (NOUN, PROPN, ADJ), 5 topics, 10 words per topic, seed 42, 50 iterations, automatic min_df/max_df. These were the settings in effect; no run in the second session changed them. An earlier run with two novels (Senilità + Una vita, about 180k words) stalled while preprocessing and the browser connection dropped. After the browser restarted, screenshot numbering began again at 001, so the first session's screenshots were overwritten. Every screen cited here comes from the second session. The custom stopwords were typed as 'cosa, volta, signore' on one line. The help tooltip asks for one word per line, so the app read the line as a single stopword and removed 0 custom tokens.

features.name: Coherence sweep over model size
features.general: Refit a model over a range of sizes, show progress, then plot the quality score against size with the current and best choices marked, and recommend a size to use in the next run
features.specific: Find optimal number of topics → Run Coherence Sweep fits LDA for k=2–15, shows 'Testing k=… (n/14)', draws a C_v line chart with 'Current: k=5' and 'Best: k=15', and tells you to change the topic count in the sidebar and run again (that re-run was not tried by either agent)
steps: expand Find optimal number of topics
press Run Coherence Sweep
watch the progress bar
read the chart and the recommended k
serves_tasks: Pick a defensible number of themes by scanning the quality score over a range

features.name: Topic inspector with chart-mode toggle, word table and representative segment
features.general: Pick one cluster from a list, view its top features as a bar chart or a word cloud, open the exact weights table, and see the most representative segment, shown as its processed lemmas
features.specific: Topics tab: Select topic dropdown, Bar chart / Word cloud radio, Word details table (Rank, Word, Weight), Representative document excerpt with the chunk ID, its topic weight and the chunk's first processed lemmas (not the raw text)
steps: choose a topic in Select topic
toggle Bar chart or Word cloud
expand Word details
expand Representative document excerpt
serves_tasks: Inspect the top words of one theme and the most representative segment, shown as its processed lemmas

features.name: Editable cluster labels that carry through all views
features.general: Replace automatic cluster names with your own and apply them everywhere at once (a reset-to-defaults control is offered but was not tried)
features.specific: Sidebar Edit topic labels (only after a run): one text field per topic, Apply labels / Reset to default; the new names appear in the Select topic dropdown and the per-topic coherence list
steps: expand Edit topic labels
type a new name for a topic
press Apply labels
check the name in Topics / Overview
serves_tasks: Give the themes meaningful names that carry through all views

features.name: Step-by-step preprocessing audit with per-token trace
features.general: Summarise how many items survive each filtering step, split counts by source file, and drill into one segment to see for every token whether each filter matched and whether it was kept
features.specific: Preprocessing tab: Preprocessing Summary metrics, Per-File Chunk Distribution table, Stopword Removal counts (built-in vs custom), a Per-document details expander (seen, not opened), and Token-level detail with a document selector and a form/lemma/pos/is_stop_builtin/is_stop_custom/pos_match/kept table
steps: open the Preprocessing tab
read the summary and stopword counts
expand Token-level detail
choose a chunk in Select document
scan the kept and filter columns
serves_tasks: Check how many tokens survived each cleaning step
Trace the fate of each individual word

features.name: Document-topic distribution with sequential (diachronic) view
features.general: Show each segment's mixture of clusters as stacked bars, then plot every cluster's weight along the order of the text, with file boundaries marked when there are several files
features.specific: Distribution tab: Document-Topic Distribution stacked bars (top 50 of 67 chunks by dominant weight) and a Diachronic View line chart of topic weight against document order, captioned 'Dashed lines mark file boundaries' (not visible with the single file used)
steps: open the Distribution tab
read the stacked proportions per chunk
scroll to the Diachronic View
follow a topic's line across the narrative
serves_tasks: Compare theme mixtures across segments and follow themes through the text in order

features.name: Topic map bubble chart (PCA fallback)
features.general: Project clusters into 2-D by PCA, size each bubble by prevalence, and hover to read the exact prevalence
features.specific: Topic Map tab: PCA scatter with bubbles coloured by topic and sized by average weight; the hover tooltip shows Topic and Prevalence. This is the fallback view; the pyLDAvis map described in the README was not shown
steps: open the Topic Map tab
compare bubble positions and sizes
hover a bubble to read its prevalence
serves_tasks: See how themes relate to each other and how large each one is

features.name: Reproducibility export bundle
features.general: Download results as separate tables or as one archive, together with a report and a record of the environment and run parameters

steps: open the Export tab
download the ZIP or the PDF report
download individual CSV/JSON files
cite the versions and parameters from environment.json, adding the applied min_df/max_df and stopwords by hand
